rv.q: Frances Poet's galvanising play, a co-production with the National Theatre of Scotland, follows in the tradition of Scottish workplace dramas such as John Byrne's The Slab Boys trilogy.
Frances Poet’s new play is vibrant, rich and full of life.

Though the script takes time to find its rhythm, the cast never misses a beat, ensuring that the defiance of the Greenock 140 isn't just a history lesson, but a living, breathing testament to industrial dignity.
This is a great show: a galvanising staging of a stirring story.

cn.t: Critics praise this propulsive gig-musical about the 1981 Lee Jeans factory occupation, with Frances Poet's storytelling and the show's energetic treatment of a landmark Scottish labor struggle earning strong notices across the board.
